How the files connect

An intro request moves from Slack to a logged outcome; the four reference tables feed the routing step by name/company text only — request_id is the sole real key.

Source: analysis/routing/routing_flow.mmd; narrative in analysis/routing/routing_flow.md.

Funnel overview

Every request drops out at the first stage it fails, so the eight buckets partition all 200 requests. Unrouted requests split on whether the target company appears in dataset/connections_*.csv; a target counts as identifiable when a company can be recovered from target_company_raw, the company names in raw_ask, or an email domain in raw_ask.

Joins you can build on

intro_outcomes.request_id -> intro_requests.request_id — 100%.Every outcome row resolves to a real request and no request_id is duplicated, so the funnel is safe to read forward from a request.
requested_by -> crm_accounts.owner — 100% / 100%.The same eight names, spelled identically, on both sides — requester-level and owner-level analysis can be mixed freely.
connector_roster.connections_file -> files on disk — 100%.Supply is fully enumerable: six rosters, six exports, 5,075 contacts.

Joins that break the analysis

target_person_raw -> connections_*.name — 0% / 0%.Not one of the 46 named individuals appears anywhere in the network (see below). Person-level routing is impossible; only the company can be matched.
connector_asked -> connector_roster.name — 54.5%.5 asks went to 5 people who are not connectors (Yusuf Petrossian, Hana Nakashima, Curtis Hartigan, Bertrand Vandermolen, Imani Mkhize), so capacity and focus-area rules never applied to them.
target_company_raw -> crm_accounts.account_name — 71.2% only after normalization.Exact match is 65.4%; the CRM side needs legal-suffix stripping to reach 84%. Every company cut below is therefore built on the resolved golden/ company id, not the raw string.
connections_*.company -> target_company_raw — 58% / 55.8%.Supply and demand barely overlap: 21 companies in the network are never requested and 23 requested companies have no contact at all.

Findings

target_person_raw is unjoinable by construction.All 46 names are distinct, none appears in 5,075 contacts, 73 investor rows, the roster, the CRM owners or as a Slack author. Every surname token, however, is a surname that does occur in the network — the names are recombinations, so any fuzzy matcher will produce plausible false positives.
The usable signal is the title, not the person.For 17 of the 46 person-named requests, a contact at the same company already holds exactly the requested title — routing should match company plus title and ignore the name.
Data point to track:target_person_resolvable = 0 / 46, target_title_reachable = 17 / 46. Recomputed on every build in dashboard/data_cuts.py.

Reading it

Routing is fast; everything after it is not.When a request is routed at all it is routed in 3.0 days on average (max 6), but the intro lands 15.7 days after the request — the delay is the connector, not the triage.
Completion is flat, not improving.Weekly volume swings between 1 and 9 requests, and the 4-week rolling completion rate stays inside 0%–36% across all 51 weeks. Month over month it never exceeds 35%.
Week-over-week trending is noisy by construction.The median week holds 4 requests, so a single intro moves the weekly rate by tens of points; the rolling line above is the honest read.

Findings

The channel is noise.316 of 323 replies repeat one of 11 stock phrases; the top 7 alone are 274 replies. Only 15 replies actually offer a path.
Offers fall through the cracks.4 of the 15 offers (R1034, R1109, R1115, R1136) have no connector_asked row — $3.8M of pipeline where someone said "leave it with me" and nothing was recorded.
Delegation never lands."adding X who might know" appears 34 times; the named person was logged as asked in 0 of them. Everyone tagged is an AE / CRM owner, not a roster connector.
Silence is not a signal.43 threads got no reply, yet 18 of them were routed to a connector anyway — the ask happened outside Slack.
Slow first response.Median 27.2 h to the first reply on the 157 threads that got one.

80 of 323 replies (25%) are someone asking whether this ask is a duplicate.They appear in 70 of the 200 threads, and only 12 of those threads ever produced an intro. Nobody ever answers the question in-thread.
The question is well-founded.86% of asks are for a company that was already requested, so "is this the same as the one from last month?" is usually yes — and the answer already exists in golden/golden_companies.csv (total_requests, latest_request_id).

"Company has a path" is measured against golden/supply_reach.csv, i.e. the network, not the flag.

Findings

path_found_flag is noise for 58% of requests.61 are blank and 55 say Unknown; of the blank ones 59% actually do have a path in the network, so blank does not mean "no path".
Where it is filled in, it contradicts the outcome.17 requests flagged Path found were never routed, and 5 flagged No path found ended in an intro. The two fields are maintained independently of the funnel.
status and the outcome rows disagree both ways.18 requests claim status Intro sent with no such outcome row, while 26 requests with a sent intro still show Open/Stalled/Routed. Neither field can be used as the funnel stage — intro_outcomes.csv has to be the source of truth.

intro_outcomes vs intro_requests — subset or coverage hole?

Status in intro_requests.csvRequests with no outcome row
Open55
Closed - no path18
Stalled15
Intro sent14
Routed13
It is a coverage hole, not a subset.All 85 outcome rows resolve to a request and none is duplicated, so the file is clean in that direction. But 27 of the 115 requests with no outcome row are filed as Routed or Intro sent ($18.3M) — a routed request must have an ask, so those rows are missing rather than not-yet-existing.
Slack shows the same gap.4 of the requests with no outcome row have someone in-thread saying they would take it — the ask happened, the row was never written.
The rest is plausibly genuine.The remaining 88 are Open, Stalled or Closed - no path, i.e. requests that legitimately never reached a connector. Treat 85/200 as the ceiling on funnel coverage and 27 as the known write-back defect.

Findings

Entity resolution is the hard part.6 groups of CRM accounts differ only by case / suffix (e.g. Ellerby Semiconductor, Inc. vs Ellerby Semiconductor), 5 of them owned by different AEs. 43 requests have no structured company and must be recovered from free text.
Connection exports need cleaning.Names with a stray leading · in every connections_*.csv; hundreds of connected_on dates pre-2020 and several in the future (up to 2028).
Inconsistent casing is systematic.requester_role, status, path_found_flag, role and account_name all mix Title / Sentence / UPPER — safe to normalise, but joins on raw strings will miss.
Outcomes are one row per request.intro_outcomes.csv has 85 rows and 85 distinct request_ids, so only one connector can ever be recorded per request.
